To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) perfect location privacy is achievable in the anonymization-obfuscation plane; (2) the region where perfect location privacy is achieved is characterized by the following: the obfuscation rate must be at least as large as the anonymization rate; and, (3) the region where no user has location is characterized by the fact that the obfuscation and anonymization rates must be at least one.

(1) perfect privacy is achievable in the i.i.d case; (2) perfect privacy is impossible in the general case; (3) the trade-off between privacy and utility can be characterized by a threshold function that depends on the underlying mobility pattern; and, (4) in the i.i.D case, the threshold function is a step function, while in the general case it is continuous.

1) perfect location privacy can be achieved for a large class of LBS systems, 2) the degree of privacy depends on the number of users and the degree to which anonymization and obfustcation are employed, and 3) there exists a threshold for each user, such that if the degree of privacy is less than that threshold, then no user has location-privacy.

the fundamental limits of location privacy under the two most common privacy protection methods, and provides a comprehensive picture of the trade-off between location privacy and utility in such systems.
